thread:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a weird tie-breaker issue in HubSpot RR when enrichment callbacks lag. Leads are sometimes skipping the pool and landing unassigned. Repro on staging.
jon: ack, thanks. Do we have a concise repro or an example lead id? :eyes:
maya: repro steps quick: create lead -> enrichment webhook delayed ~4s -> RR assignment runs on created_at -> enrichment arrives with buyer intent -> final assign step tries to set owner but fails because RR already advanced. Seen ~30% of traffic in staging.
liam: can you paste the webhook/assignment logs for one example?
maya: sure, here's a trimmed trace from staging:
```
[1765439876] Lead created id=stg-7721
[1765439877] RR assignment started pool=sdrcore slot=4 -> assigned candidate=alice (tentative)
[1765439879] POST /webhooks/enrichment 200 body_delay=4200ms payload={"lead_id":"stg-7721","score":0.82}
[1765439880] RR advance -> candidate alice timed out -> owner set to null
[1765439881] Enrichment callback processed -> assign_by_score attempted -> conflict_owner=none -> persisted owner=null
```
hubspot-bot: POST /webhooks/enrichment delivered 1765439879 status=200
liam: ok that matches a race. Two options: (A) change HubSpot workflow to wait for enrichment when possible (hold window), or (B) make the assign-by-score step idempotent / retry-friendly so it can claim even if RR moved on.
emma: curious — what's our handoff SLA threshold again? SalesOps is hoping <2s assignment for inbound for lead routing dashboards. If we add a wait, could break that. :confused:
maya: correct SLA is 2s for visible owner assignment, but we currently have a 30s fallback window where unowned leads trigger followups. Most customers expect near-instant but tolerates short hold.
liam: proposed small change to minimize surface area: implement a short tie-break hold of 2s, only if enrichment is flagged as pending. Pseudocode for a HubSpot workflow condition below:
```
# HubSpot assignment pseudo-rule
if lead.enrichment_status == 'pending' and now - lead.created_at < 2000:
  delay_assignment(2000)
else:
  assign_round_robin()
```
elena: can we do that as a canary in one region first? Also we should add a telemetry counter: increments when "hold path" taken and when final assignment remains unowned after 10s.
jon: agreed. Plan: canary EU region for 24h with metrics and auto-rollback if unowned_rate > baseline + 0.5%. Who owns the HubSpot workflow edit + telemetry?
liam: I can open the PR for the HubSpot workflow template + an accompanying Change in infra that emits hold_path / final_unowned metrics to cloud-metrics. Will also add a quick retry guard to assign-by-score so it attempts acquisition for 1s after enrichment arrives.
maya: perfect. Can you include a smoke test that creates leads with intentional enrichment delays? We should automate and gate on the owner visible in UI within 10s.
liam: yes — test plan in PR will create 50 leads with random enrichment delays [0ms..5000ms] and assert unowned_rate < 1%.
emma: from Ops/Sales side, please add a runbook note: if hold-path spikes, disable hold and notify SalesOps channel. Also update handoff docs so SDRs know to refresh list if assignment momentarily delayed.
jon: timeline: liam opens PR today, run the canary tomorrow, monitor for 24h, then iterate. cc @elena for telemetry dashboard. :thumbsup:
elena: noted — I'll add dashboard tiles: hold_path_rate, post_enrichment_claim_success, final_unowned_rate. Will set alert at +0.5% from baseline.
maya: thanks team. tagging this for follow-up in tomorrow standup. :rocket:
